subject: Performance SLO & Load test next steps (recap)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@financecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & Load test next steps (recap)

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Feel free to correct anything I mis-captured.

Key SLOs / requirements (as discussed)
- P95 latency target: <= 200ms for non-streaming responses (JSON)
- Streaming responses: target p95 of <= 300ms per chunk; support chunked HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 streaming.
- Concurrency: sustained ~250 concurrent user sessions, spike testing up to ~400 concurrent sessions for 5-10m windows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~150 req/s, short-term peaks to ~400 req/s.
- Failure tolerance: graceful degradation with 429s under sustained overload; prefer early-failover behavior.

Customer-led load test coordination items
- Redwood to provide an initial k6 script and a sample Locustfile (we'll include both options). (Owner: Marissa)
- FinanceCorp to confirm preferred runner (k6 cloud / k6 OSS / Locust) and test window. (Owner: Alex)
- Redwood to provision a test account + API key and provide IP allowlist CSV for your firewall. (Owner: Logan)
- Agree on metrics capture: we recommend p95/p99 latency, error rates, and per-connection KB/s for streaming. (Owner: Rishi)

Proposed test window
- Apr 18, 2027 09:00-11:00 UTC (2 hour window) — targets, ramp, and ramp-down plan attached in the loadtest-plan.pdf.

Attachments: loadtest-plan.pdf (1 page plan with ramp profiles)

Next steps (TL;DR)
- Alex: confirm runner preference and confirm SRE persona to include on firewall reqs (who will provide IP allowlist on your side).
- Marissa: will share k6 + Locust samples and create the test account + send IP ranges.
- Logan/Rishi: stand by for the test; we'll send Gradual rollouts and a fallback plan for any production impacts.

Thanks 
Logan Wright
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@financecorp.com>

On Sun, 11 Apr 2027 at 10:15 AM Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call this morning — quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Thanks for the recap, Logan — this looks right to me. A couple clarifying points from the SRE side:
- Streaming transport: we actually prefer HTTP/2 streaming (we use HTTP/2 + chunked responses in prod). Will Redwood's streaming path support HTTP/2?
- Runner preference: our SRE team prefers Locust for load test orchestration (we have an existing harness), but k6 is fine if you think it exercises the same code paths. If you can provide both samples that'd be ideal.
- Test accounts: we'll need an API key associated with an account that has production-like data scopes but is throttled to not touch billing systems.
- Firewall: I added Nora here (nora.park@financecorp.com) — she'll handle whitelisting. We'll need a CSV or list of public egress IPs from Redwood so we can add to the firewall.

We can tentatively lock Apr 18 09:00-11:00 UTC; Nora will confirm final window once she checks change calendar.

Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
FinanceCorp

Alex / Nora — adding the artifacts you asked for.

What I'm attaching / sharing now:
- k6_script_v1.js (attached) — baseline script that hits the /v1/generate and /v1/stream endpoints with a mix of prompt sizes.
- ip-allowlist.csv (attached) — three public egress ranges we expect requests to come from for the test window. Please confirm these are acceptable; we can provide additional ranges if you want a managed NAT pool.
- Shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/FinanceCorp/loadtest/k6_script_v1.js (k6 + runbook)

Test account / credentials
- Test account created: financecorp-loadtest@redwood-test
- API key: (sensitive) — we'll send the API key over the secure key channel / 1Password; don't paste keys in-line here.

Notes about the scripts
- k6 script exercises both streaming and non-streaming paths; streaming uses HTTP/1.1 chunked by default in this sample. If you require HTTP/2 streaming, we can provide a Locust example that uses the requests library with HTTP/2 support.
- Ramp profile in loadtest-plan.pdf: 5m ramp to 150 req/s, hold for 90m (we'll shorten to match your 2h window), 5m ramp to 400 req/s for a 5-10m spike, then ramp down.

Attachments: k6_script_v1.js, ip-allowlist.csv

If Locust is preferred, we can convert the k6 scenario or provide a Locustfile by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 1:18 PM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex / Nora — adding the artifacts you asked for.

Thanks, Marissa — receiving the k6 script and IP list. A few quick items from SRE: 
- We'll run the test with Locust (we have an existing cluster and LB profiles). k6 is fine too, but Locust gives us better control over user scenarios. If you can provide a Locustfile, that would be great; otherwise we'll convert your k6 scenario locally.
- Please confirm the public egress IP ranges we should open on our firewall; I see ip-allowlist.csv attached — we'll need the definitive list by Wed EOD to avoid change window conflicts.
- Test window: Apr 18 09:00-11:00 UTC works for us tentatively; Alex to confirm change calendar. We'll run a small smoke test 30 minutes before the window to validate the API key and routes.

Request for Redwood (action items)
- Provide Locustfile or a Locust-ready manifest compatible with our runner.
- Confirm if streaming path will be available over HTTP/2 — we prefer HTTP/2 for this test.
- Send the API key via secure channel and confirm the account will not have write access to billing or production-critical systems.

We'll reply with firewall change ticket ID once we schedule the change. Looking forward to the run.

Best,
Nora Park
Senior SRE Manager
FinanceCorp
